Subject: SIG follow-up — tenancy assertions we need

Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving through the SIG/CAIQ and have a short list of evidence items we need to close our internal review. To be efficient, could you provide a concise "zero-trust tenancy assertions" doc (one page + annexes) that answers the following at a minimum:  

- How Dedicated vs Private deployments isolate tenant control plane metadata (where customer identifiers live).
- Network egress controls and how we enforce customer-specific egress (NAT, egress IPs, firewall rules).
- KV/cache separation for inference workloads and whether cross-tenant residues are possible.
- KMS boundaries — do customer keys ever transit Redwood-managed hardware?

If you have a short network diagram that maps control-plane and data-plane flows for both Dedicated and Private, that would be ideal. Ideally we get this in the next 48 hours — we're trying to sign off this sprint.

Thanks,

Daniel

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-11T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: draft assertions & artifacts (for ACME)

Team —

I've drafted the assertions and pulled the diagram from the infra team. Key callouts included in the draft:  

- Control plane metadata: customer IDs and routing tables are stored in a customer-scoped control DB that lives in the Private control plane when deployed in VPC mode; for Dedicated we run a customer-dedicated control plane instance in the tenant pool (no shared control-plane indices). Statement added: "No shared control-plane indices across tenants."
- Data plane flows: inference payloads traverse a per-tenant network namespace and are served by dedicated or pinned inference pools depending on Dedicated/Private selection. Diagram shows per-tenant SGs and per-pool load balancers.
- KV/cache: We use per-tenant cache namespaces with deterministic eviction; cache keys include tenant prefixes. Backing cache is segmented per-pool with ACLs; we assert "no cross-tenant cache access in production" and include the cache-segmentation config excerpt.
- KMS: For Private deployments customers can bring their own KMS; keys never leave the customer's KMS. For Dedicated (hosted on Redwood infra) we integrate with customer KMS via KMIP or cloud-KMS; we never persist plaintext keys and HSM is used for signing when configured.

I've attached:  
- redwood_zero-trust_assertions_v1.pdf (one-page + annex)
- network-diagram-dedicated-private.svg (labelled flows)
- vpn-egress-matrix.csv (list of egress IP blocks and service ports)

Action items: Karthik, please add a short SOC2/SIG crosswalk paragraph referencing our SOC2 controls for change management and network segmentation. Priyom, please sanity-check the egress matrix (cloud provider NAT ranges).

Kimberly Park
Security Architect | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@acme-cloud.com>, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-12T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — tenancy assertions we need

Daniel —

Attaching the requested package here (see attachments in Rafael's mailbox copy). Short SOC2/SIG crosswalk:  

- Network segmentation: Covered by CC3 (Logical & Physical Access Controls) and CC7 (Change Management) in our SOC2 scope; we reference control ids R-INF-SEG-01 (per-tenant SGs) and R-INF-PL-02 (segmented cache namespaces).  
- Evidence: network diagrams, ACL extracts, cache namespace config, KMS integration notes, and egress NAT listing.

We assert the following succinctly for SIG: "Redwood enforces tenant isolation using per-tenant network namespaces and segregated control plane instances for Dedicated customers; caches and KV stores are namespaced and access-controlled; customer-managed KMS keys remain under customer control in Private deployments and are never exported in plaintext from hardware HSMs."

Let us know if you'd like us to convert the one-page assertion into a signed letter on Redwood letterhead. Happy to do that if it speeds your procurement.

Thanks —

Karthik Iyer
Head of Compliance | Redwood Inference
